The log effect reads count() and a computed derived from it and writes the log via log.peek(); on 2.3.2 one set() settles computeds and runs the effect exactly once (including under batch()), so the original BN-1 diamond fix was not needed and no equivalent fix is counted.

react.harnessFixNote: R2-1 (tooling, react/build.mjs): the task-2 stdin entry pointed at ./react/task2/app.jsx but its resolveDir was already the react/ directory, so esbuild could not resolve it and react/dist/task2.mjs was never emitted (task-2 test failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Fixed the entry path to ./task2/app.jsx; the suite then passed 4/4. Documented translations applied in the first pass and not counted: R-2 (navigator via Object.defineProperty), the R-3-family 50 ms macrotask settle instead of act() (the bundled copy has its own React), and the controlled-input native prototype setter.

reactBuildToolingOneTime.note: One-time hand-written build script React needed in this repo; BaseNative needed no equivalent. Counted once in the amortization, not per task.

agentDocsBundle.note: One-time LLM context cost for BaseNative, measured on the repo's current shipped agent docs bundle (llms.txt + docs/llm/START.md in the canonical BaseNative clone). React needs no equivalent (its API is in model weights).

amortization.explanation: No break-even exists at this task size: the average per-task code-token saving is -32.5 (negative — BaseNative code was slightly LARGER than React code on these two small tasks), so the one-time docs cost of 2933 net tokens is never recovered through per-task code-size savings. The docs bundle pays off through avoided syntax errors and zero build/tooling friction (see RUN_LOG_REFRESH.md), not through smaller code. Larger, template-heavy tasks may change the per-task sign; these two tasks do not show it.
